key_insight: DeGG-Flow adds decoupled guidance to multi-agent flow matching so each agent can satisfy hard shared or private constraints without needing synchronized guidance from others.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables constraint-aware generative modeling for robotics and scene generation, making it useful for safety-critical multi-agent systems that must produce valid configurations under hard requirements.
method: Model generation as a control-affine dynamical system.
Derive guidance conditions for shared constraints across agents and private constraints tied to individual agents and neighbors.
Prove feasibility, finite-horizon convergence, and a Wasserstein bound on distributional deviation caused by guidance.
evidence_signal: The paper demonstrates the method on multi-robot gap crossing via environment reconfiguration and on multi-object scene generation with affordance constraints, including team sizes not seen during training.
watch_item: Guarantees depend on the stated feasibility conditions and the guidance design, so performance may degrade if constraints are incompatible or the learned dynamics poorly approximate the target distribution.
paper_title: Multi-Agent Flow Matching with Decoupled Generative Guidance
